The morning opens like a quiet door in the mind.
I hear water moving somewhere behind the walls of today.
A small bird repeats one bright note until it fades.
The street below carries people toward lives I never know.
Every window holds a different weather, a different private season.
I think about all the words I failed to say.
They gather in my throat like stones learning to sing.
Perhaps silence is just another country we visit while waiting.
The kettle clicks, and the kitchen fills with warm grass.
A spoon rests on the counter, remembering heat and morning.

The table accepts my elbows, my book, my wandering attention.
Outside, a truck passes, dragging a chain of distant thunder.
I wonder where the night goes when it is replaced.
Maybe it folds itself into drawers, socks, and closed eyes.
Maybe it hides in the spaces between ordinary blue cups.
I once loved a person whose laughter sounded like rain.
I once lost a key that opened no important door.
The important doors stayed with me, patient as wooden trees.
There is a chair where my coat becomes a guest.
There is a mirror where my face becomes a question.

I answer it by washing a plate, then another plate.
Soap bubbles hold tiny worlds that vanish when I touch.
Perhaps we are all brief reflections looking for a window.
The afternoon leans against the wall, wearing gold and dust.
A child shouts a name, and the whole street turns.
For one second, everyone belongs to the same sudden story.
Then the moment breaks into errands, keys, and weather again.
I buy apples without understanding why they seem like hope.
The shopkeeper smiles as if kindness is a daily habit.
I carry the bag home, feeling the weight of things.

On the stairs, my shadow practices being someone older now.
I let it lead, because darkness sometimes knows the way.
Inside, the quiet room keeps its patient collection of light.
The shelf remembers every object I placed there and forgot.
A ticket from a journey rests like a sleeping leaf.
I touch its edge and hear a train arriving again.
Someone I used to be waves from the platform smiling.
I do not call out, because he cannot hear me.
The past is a station we leave behind us always.
The future is a train we still wait for today.

Night arrives gently, placing blue coins over the windows outside.
The city breathes in neon, smoke, and tired songs together.
Somewhere a door closes with the softness of snow falling.
Somewhere a letter begins its slow journey toward honesty again.
I imagine envelopes trembling in the hands of strangers tonight.
Words can be small animals seeking warmth across distance together.
I write to say I was here, listening all along.
I write to keep ordinary things from disappearing completely now.
The clock makes a tiny house for seconds to live.
Each tick opens a room we have not entered yet.

I remember my mother singing while the rain waited outside.
Her voice was a lantern made of simple air then.
My father fixed chairs and spoke in measured lines always.
He taught me that silence can be a tool too.
I grew tall beside the refrigerator and the calendar there.
Months changed like pictures inside a slow theater of years.
The kitchen smelled of bread, metal, and winter evening light.
I was afraid of dogs and of being forgotten often.
I was also afraid of becoming someone careless and cold.
Now I try to greet the day politely each morning.

I open the curtains like a small ceremony of hope.
The sky is wearing its ordinary blue coat again today.
People pass beneath it with bread and worries in bags.
A dog sniffs the secret history of the sidewalk outside.
The wind rearranges papers into a false poem for me.
I read it anyway, because mistakes can shine at night.
Maybe every life is a draft with music hidden inside.
We correct the lines until they sound true together now.
The truth is not always pretty, but it helps us.
It sits beside us like a dog in rain waiting.

I think of rivers moving under bridges of traffic above.
Fish carry silver messages through the dark water below us.
The moon practices its reflection, failing beautifully all night long.
I try to practice patience, failing beautifully too most days.
A plant on the sill forgives my forgetting it again.
It lifts one green hand toward the window every day.
I should learn such quiet ambition from leaves somehow now.
They make sugar from light and ask for little else.
My hands want to build, hold, and repair things again.
My heart wants to be a small warm house too.

Some nights, loneliness is a chair facing itself quietly there.
I sit with it until it becomes company again soon.
The refrigerator hums a lullaby for leftover fruit below me.
The faucet drips one bright bead after another all night.
I fix what I can and leave the rest alone.
That is a kind of wisdom, perhaps, but small enough.
There are people who make rooms easier to enter alone.
There are people who make silence feel like bread shared.
I hope I have been one of them sometimes too.
I hope my presence has been a gentle weather too.

Tomorrow will arrive with its list of necessary things again.
I will answer messages and pretend to understand time better.
I will drink coffee and mistake it for courage again.
I will watch clouds perform their slow white theater outside.
I will forget some kindness and remember some regret too.
Then evening will place its hand on the rooftops quietly.
The day will fold into drawers, socks, and closed eyes.
I will listen for water moving behind the walls again.
Maybe this is enough: to notice, to continue, to write.
The morning opens like a quiet door, and I enter.
